detail: Sheet FERNANDO legend: black=1st, dark red=2nd, green=3rd, blue=4th, purple=5th, orange=6th, dark blue=7th, red 2=8th, light green=9th. Sheet7 legend differs (blue=1st, red=2nd, green=3rd, black=4th, violet=5th, yellow=6th, orange=7th). Sheet7 is an earlier draft.

Rows "#2..Faustina Ynot" and "#3..Basilia" (after Marcos Valiente Muñasque's descendants) and "#..Sarip Arabia Omar" (after Cosmiano's descendants) are coloured in a special red. They are read as 2nd/3rd partners of Marcos and 2nd partner of Cosmiano because their children are coloured 3rd generation and because Sheet5/Sheet8 place them inside those branches. An alternative reading, that they were later wives of the progenitor Fernando, would make their children 2nd generation; the colours argue against it.

Rows 949–1044 (Marcos branch) are coloured one or two levels too deep and inconsistently; e.g. Purification P. Muñasque is blue (4th) although she is a child of a 2nd-generation person. Text labels and naming convention were used instead; Palexina Perez Muñasque and Col. Coronado Perez Muñasque ("Perez" = mother Matilde Perez) are placed as children of Marcos (3rd generation), one level higher than the compiler's label.

Several people whose middle name shows their mother's surname were placed by the compiler under a sibling instead of their parents (e.g. Czar, Ruth and Dr. Quintin Jr. Muñasque Salimbangon under Thelma; Wilfredo, Raquel, Sarah and Cezar Franco A. Muñasque under Samuel A.; Leonardo, Restituto and Sergio Muñasque Pino under Demetrio; Eliezar, Teresita and Dominador E. Muñasque under Felixberto). Re-attached to the parents implied by the naming convention; the branch sheets (S2) agree in each case checked. All such moves are listed in overrides.csv with reasons.

Alice/Alicia, Perla, Leonillo/Leonilo and Sonia Salimbangon carry the initial P. in the master sheet but G. (Gelig) in Sheet3. Treated as children of Teodulfo & Felipa Gelig per Sheet3. A second wife beginning with P. cannot be excluded.
Press (2006) says Milagros Lago Salimbangon had seven children; spreadsheet lists eight (Aida, Ofelia, Benhur, Cesar, Mariquita, Danilo, Edwin, Freddie).
best_supported_reading: unresolved; press count may exclude a deceased child or the spreadsheet may include a non-child

detail: First pass gave Glan (Colony No. 9) as "surveyed c. 1912"; the fact-check found it was founded in 1914 by Cebu pioneers under Tranquilino Ruiz (first settlers 8 Oct 1914). Corrected.

First pass cited A.M. No. P-227 (30 Sep 1974) as the case naming Benjamin N. Muñasque; the fact-check shows P-227 was his own complaint, dismissed on that date, and that the decision naming him as Clerk of Court is A.M. No. P-145 (31 Oct 1974). The 1979 case (G.R. L-28485) was not re-found. Citations corrected.

The first NLSA settlers landed at Sarangani Bay on 27 Feb 1939, before Commonwealth Act 441 chartered the NLSA on 3 Jun 1939: Gen. Paulino Santos had been appointed its general manager in Jan 1939 and the settlement began administratively. Sulpicio Muñasque arrived on 7 Mar 1939, eight days after the first landing.

best_supported_reading: unresolved; a civil or church record would settle it

Children carrying the mother's surname and the mother's own middle name (e.g. Roberto M. Cosip under Esperanza Muñasque Cosip; Samantha Jean M. Muñasque under Jojo C. Muñasque; Princess Justine S. Muñasque under Elena S. Muñasque; Jona Girl Muñasque and Cyril M. Ochotorena under Rosalia A. Muñasque) follow the Philippine practice of registering a child under the mother's name. Kept as the compiler placed them; flagged low confidence.

Some women are entered under married surnames (Leonarda Y. Booc, Vivian G. Caballes, Eva Muñasque Jo, Delilah Stevens Carey); their middle initials show the maiden line. Leonarda is shown as Muñasque with Booc recorded as a variant.
Children of Malapat Muñasque Tambingag & Tarhata Marohombsar carry "T." (apparently for Tarhata, the mother's given name), a Maranao/Maguindanao usage, not a Hispanic maiden-surname initial.
Adelfa and Leoncio Muñasque Etcuban (rows 1232–1234) and Teresita Go with the Grande family (rows 590–593) are entered twice; Rosalinda B. Etcuban twice (1252, 1285). Second copies dropped.

detail: Two hypotheses: (a) the oral story recorded by the compiler (S3) that Muñasque was formed from the names Mukilan, Anañas and Roque; (b) a Claveria-catalogue origin, now supported by an OCR entry "monasque/moñasque" on page 87 of the 1849 Catálogo (S53). Neither is proven: (b) needs the page image checked and does not say which Opon family took the name; (a) has no documentary trace and does not explain the Spanish-looking ending.
best_supported_reading: catalogue origin somewhat better supported; verify on scan

detail: The compiler places the family at Opon, Cebu (S3, residence column "OPON, CEBU" in S2). The Salimbangon branch that produced Congressman Benhur lived in Curva, Medellin (northern Cebu). How Agripina Valiente Muñasque's family came to Medellin is undocumented.
